run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T02:54:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy fires because frontend-proxy intermittently returns HTTP 503 to clients: Envoy access logs show `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` toward its upstream cluster `frontend` (Service ClusterIP 100.71.221.228:8080). The pattern is sporadic (roughly 1–3 events per minute), appears in readable proxy logs from 02:24:16Z through 03:02:27Z, and is confirmed in traces: frontend-proxy `ingress` spans carry error=true/http.status_code=503 while the paired `router frontend egress` span has error=true and http.status_code=0, and the failed trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 contains no `frontend` spans at all — the upstream never started a response. The dependency was investigated: the single `frontend` pod (100.96.3.42, one Service endpoint) is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its p95 request latency is flat at ~180–225 ms, and its own error spans are essentially zero except one 5-minute bucket around 02:49Z. So the reset is a connection-termination at the frontend socket/server level, not an application error rate or latency collapse. Two observations remain hypotheses rather than proven causes: (a) frontend runs under a 100m CPU / 200Mi memory limit with ~26–32% of CFS periods throttled and a working set of ~239–262 MB (above the 200Mi limit), which is a plausible contributing condition but is not temporally correlated with the 503s; (b) the resets behave like upstream connection-lifecycle (keep-alive) races that began as load ramped from ~3.25 to ~10 requests/s. A separate change in the window, the product-catalog pod replacement at 02:46:57–02:47:01Z, coincides with a brief burst of frontend-side `tcp.connect`/`dns.lookup` errors near 02:49Z but cannot explain 503s that started ~22 minutes earlier and continued afterwards.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emits error spans on two operations, `ingress` and `router frontend egress`, with status codes limited to STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the `ingress` error spans carry http.status_code=503 and the paired `router frontend egress` spans carry error=true with http.status_code=0.

frontend-proxy access logs record HTTP 503 with Envoy flag `UC` and detail `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` against upstream cluster `frontend` (host 100.71.221.228:8080, the frontend Service ClusterIP), with the downstream client being the load-generator pod at 100.96.3.52.

Trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 contains only four spans — load-generator `user_browse_product` and `GET` (503), frontend-proxy `ingress` (503) and `router frontend egress` (error, http.status_code=0) — with no `frontend` service span, i.e. the proxied request never produced an application response.

The frontend-proxy error rate measured over all its spans is small: the error/total span ratio stays between ~0.00019 and ~0.00275, and per-operation rates show `ingress` STATUS_CODE_ERROR around 0.0037–0.033 spans/s against ~10 spans/s of STATUS_CODE_UNSET `ingress` spans.

The upstream `frontend` is healthy at the pod level: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, IP 100.96.3.42, and the `frontend` Service (ClusterIP 100.71.221.228, port 8080) has exactly one endpoint address, that same pod.

frontend request latency did not degrade: p95 of frontend server spans (GET /api/products/*, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart) stays at ~173–226 ms throughout 02:25–03:05Z, so the 503s are not accompanied by an upstream latency increase.

frontend runs with CPU limit 100m and memory limit 200Mi, and is resource-constrained: the container is throttled in ~26–32% of CFS periods (frontend-proxy only ~2.6–5.5%), and its memory working set is ~239.7 MB to ~262.3 MB, i.e. above the 200Mi limit, without any container restart.

frontend's own error spans are near zero and concentrated in a single 5-minute bucket around 02:49Z, where STATUS_CODE_ERROR appears on span_name GET (~0.0185/s), POST (~0.0037/s), POST /api/checkout and executing api route /api/checkout (~0.0037/s) and tcp.connect (~0.0037/s), with dns.lookup (~0.0074/s) present as STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

A product-catalog pod replacement occurred inside the window: Deployment product-catalog scaled up new ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 at 02:46:57Z (pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started) and scaled down product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc at 02:47:01Z, whose pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp was deleted. Both ReplicaSet templates declare the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, the same env vars and the same cpu 15m/memory 30Mi resources.

Within 02:50:00–03:00:00Z the only 5xx responses in frontend-proxy logs were the 503/UC ones; lines matching 500, 502, 504, UF, UH or 'no healthy' were only four 200-status requests whose logged durations happened to contain those digits, so no 504/UF-type upstream timeout or no-healthy-endpoint failure was observed in that interval.

The 503s are upstream connection-lifecycle (keep-alive / idle-connection reset) races rather than an application failure: the request is reset before any response header, no frontend span is created, latency is flat, and first appearance (02:24:16Z) coincides with frontend-proxy ingress traffic ramping from ~3.25 spans/s to ~10 spans/s after the load-generator started; no requests in readable logs before 02:24:16 show the 503/UC pattern.

The frontend container's tight resource envelope (CPU limit 100m with ~26–32% of periods throttled, memory working set above the 200Mi limit) is a plausible contributing condition that leaves the Node/Next.js server slow or unable to service reused connections, but it is steady across the whole window and therefore is not shown to be the trigger of individual resets.

Separately from the 503s, the brief frontend-side connect/DNS error burst near 02:49Z (tcp.connect ERROR, dns.lookup, GET/POST ERROR) coincides in time with the product-catalog pod replacement at 02:46:57–02:47:01Z; this is time correlation only — the error spans do not name their target dependency, and Jaeger holds no traces from that moment to confirm it.

The alert annotation's current value 0.011111... equals 1/90, consistent with a single 503 among about 90 requests in a short evaluation window; the alerting rule `RequestErrorRate` itself could not be retrieved from this Prometheus, so its exact expression remains unverified.

The product-catalog rollout at 02:46:57–02:47:01Z did not cause the RequestErrorRate alert: identical 503/UC upstream resets are already logged from 02:24:16Z (about 22 minutes before the rollout) and continue after it to at least 03:02:27Z, and frontend latency is unchanged through the rollout.

frontend shows no sustained application-level failure that would by itself explain a 1.1% error rate: 0 container restarts, Ready pod, a single Service endpoint, flat p95 latency, and error spans confined to one 5-minute bucket; likewise frontend-proxy itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and only ~2.6–5.5% CPU throttling.

To close the remaining gap, align the frontend-proxy upstream idle/keep-alive settings with the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive timeout (and consider enabling upstream retries for 503 connection resets), and raise frontend's CPU (100m) and memory (200Mi) limits so throttling and the above-limit working set stop; then confirm the 503/UC rate drops in frontend-proxy access logs.

gaps: frontend application logs could not be read at all: for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw the log stream returned 0 lines/0 bytes for every window tried (02:30–03:10, 02:35–02:36, 03:05–03:14), so the reason the frontend closes connections is not observable from its own output.

The alerting rule `RequestErrorRate` is not present in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no data for that rule name), so the exact metric/label expression and evaluation window behind the 0.011111 value are unverified.

No baseline before the incident: traces_span_metrics_calls_total for frontend-proxy has no samples before ~02:25Z, and readable frontend-proxy logs start at 02:14:00Z (first 503 seen at 02:24:16Z), so a longer pre-incident error baseline is unknown.

kube_pod_container_info returned no data, so the image digests (image_id) of the old product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp and the new pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 could not be compared; only the identical declared image tag/env/resources of the two ReplicaSets could be compared.

Jaeger retains only recent traces (trace data seen up to ~02:42Z); the frontend error bucket around 02:49Z has no traces, so the dependency targeted by the frontend tcp.connect/dns.lookup failures is unknown.

frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration (upstream idle timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retry policy) is not observable — no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in the namespace (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector, product-catalog-products) and the config appears baked into the image.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so whether frontend/frontend-proxy manifests, limits or load-generator settings changed shortly before the first 503 at ~02:24Z is unknown.
The reason for frontend's memory working set exceeding its declared 200Mi limit without an OOMKill/restart is unexplained by the available metrics.
next_steps: Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster config (idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retry_on) with the frontend Next.js HTTP keep-alive/headers timeout, and align them.

Raise the frontend Deployment resources (cpu limit 100m, memory limit 200Mi) or remove the limits, then watch container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total/container_cpu_cfs_periods_total and the 503 UC rate in frontend-proxy logs.
Collect frontend container stdout (currently empty via the log tool) or enable its access/error logging so upstream connection terminations can be attributed inside the application.

Review the product-catalog Deployment revision history for the 02:46:57Z rollout (what pod-template field changed) and confirm whether frontend's brief 02:49Z connect/DNS errors were caused by that endpoint replacement.
Confirm the RequestErrorRate rule definition and evaluation window in the Alertmanager/Prometheus that actually owns it, since the rule is absent from this target's Prometheus.
